title: Exact Mayer--Vietoris segment for module-sheaf pullbacks
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $i:Z\to X$ a morphism of schemes, $J$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $X$, $U,V\subseteq X$ opens with $U\cup V=X$, and $r\in\mathbb N$. With the scheme and site conventions [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], let $F$ be the underlying abelian sheaf of $i^*J$, and $F_T$ the underlying abelian sheaf of $\operatorname{pr}_1^*(T.\iota^*J)$ on $T\times_XZ$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. There exist additive homomorphisms $\delta:H^r(F_{U\cap V})\to H^{r+1}(F)$ and $\rho:H^{r+1}(F)\to H^{r+1}(F_U)\times H^{r+1}(F_V)$ such that $\operatorname{im}\delta=\ker\rho$, where cohomology is Sheaf.H [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No vanishing hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Two-open long exact sequence, transported via inverse-image composition and underlying abelian sheaves (Tags 03D3 and 03D7).

proof.text: For each open T, use Mathlib pullbackSymmetry followed by pullbackRestrictIsoRestrict to identify T ×_X Z with the inverse-image open. Its inverse composed with the first projection is the restriction of i; morphismRestrict_ι gives the equality of composites. These are the direct Mathlib implementations of base change of open immersions and identification with their image.

The private proved helper module_open_pullback_cohomology_equiv applies three upperStarComp isomorphisms to identify the transported module sheaf with the restriction of i^*J. Apply sheafCompose.mapIso, and twice pullback_forget_modules_iso. Apply Sheaf.functorH.mapIso to the resulting abelian-sheaf isomorphism. Compose its additive equivalence with cohomologyEquiv along the inverse scheme isomorphism.

Let F be the underlying abelian sheaf of i^*J. Inverse image preserves sup and top, so the inverse-image opens cover Z. Apply etale_mayerVietoris_pullback to this cover and the identity of Z; use only its first sequence, already expressed in Sheaf.H, and extract exactness of δ_r followed by the product of restrictions in degree r+1.

Precompose δ_r with the intersection equivalence, and postcompose each restriction with the inverse of its open equivalence. If the new restriction pair is zero, injectivity of the inverse equivalences makes the old pair zero; exactness supplies y, whose inverse intersection image is the required preimage. Conversely old exactness makes both restrictions of δ_r(e_I(y)) zero; applying the inverse open equivalences still gives zero. This proves Function.Exact for the displayed additive homomorphisms.
